title: ../aoc 2018/06 manhattan silently returns 0 after the HardWrap (.-.) fix
description:
BREAKING CONSUMER CHANGE, confirmed empirically against the fixed library.

sized-grid-0kf removed the 'max 0' clamp from HardWrap's (.-.) so it returns a true
signed displacement. ../aoc/src/2018/06.hs:22-26 was relying on that clamp to compute
an absolute value:

    manhattan c1 c2 = fromIntegral $ sum [dx1, dx2, dy1, dy2]
      where
        (dx1, dy1) = c1 .-. c2
        (dx2, dy2) = c2 .-. c1

OLD: dx1 = max 0 (x1-x2), dx2 = max 0 (x2-x1), so dx1 + dx2 = |x1-x2|. Correct.
NEW: dx1 = x1-x2, dx2 = x2-x1, so dx1 + dx2 = 0. Always.

Probe output against the fixed library (HardWrap 400 x HardWrap 400):
    (1,1) -> (8,3) = 0
    (8,3) -> (1,1) = 0
    (5,5) -> (5,5) = 0
    (3,4) -> (8,9) = 0

Every distance is 0, so 2018/06 produces a wrong answer rather than failing loudly.

FIX (in ../aoc, one line):

    manhattan c1 c2 = fromIntegral $ sum $ map abs [dx, dy]
      where (dx, dy) = c1 .-. c2

This is a defect in the consumer, not a reason to revert sized-grid-0kf: the old
behaviour violated the AffineSpace round-trip law and the clamp-as-abs trick only
worked by accident. But ../aoc must be patched in the same change set, or its 2018/06
answer regresses silently.

Also re-check the moorePoints call sites, which the 0kf fix was expected to IMPROVE:
  - ../aoc/src/2025/04.hs:62 'filter (/= coord) . nubOrd . moorePoints 1'
  - ../aoc/src/2015/18.hs:51 and ../aoc/src/2018/18.hs:67 (both commented out)
The nubOrd workarounds may now be removable; verify before deleting them.
close_reason: Fixed ../aoc/src/2018/06.hs manhattan to take abs of a single signed diff; verified against the day's own (17,90) doctest via a scratch replica run in cabal repl, since ../aoc cannot build here (hmatrix/blas). moorePoints follow-up recorded on sized-grid-7gs: nubOrd workarounds must stay.

comments.author: Kevin Horlick
comments.text:
FIXED in ../aoc/src/2018/06.hs. manhattan is now:

    manhattan c1 c2 = fromIntegral $ sum $ map abs [dx, dy]
      where (dx, dy) = c1 .-. c2

Verification: ../aoc cannot be built in this environment (pre-existing, unrelated:
hmatrix-0.20.2 fails to configure, 'Missing (or bad) C libraries: blas, lapack', and
every aoc executable depends on it). So the day was replicated verbatim against the
fixed library in a scratch module and run through 'cabal repl sized-grid':

    expected      : (17,90)   <- the doctest at ../aoc/src/2018/06.hs:42-43
    new manhattan : (17,90)   PASS
    old manhattan : *** Exception: Data.Foldable.maximum (for Data.IntMap): empty map

Correction to this issue's description: 2018/06 did not silently return a wrong
answer, it CRASHED. With every distance 0 the first target wins on 0 < maxBound and
every later one compares EQ, so closestIndex marks a tie and ownerGrid is all Nothing;
'areas' is then the empty IntMap and 'maximum areas' throws. The distances were indeed
all 0 (probe: (1,1)->(8,3) = 0 old, 9 new), the description was only wrong about the
failure being silent.

title: WIP gridWindows: rows work, but 'mapLowerDim gridWindows' for columns/squares takes a cartesian product
description:
Applies to the uncommitted change in src/SizedGrid/Grid/Grid.hs:258-266 and its use in
sudoko/src/Main.hs:50-59.

CONFIRMED with a 4x4 stand-in for the 9x9 board:

    rows    = gridWindows board                 -- 4 results, correct
    columns = mapLowerDim gridWindows board     -- 256 results, expected 4

The first six 'columns' produced were
    [1,5,9,13] [1,5,9,14] [1,5,9,15] [1,5,9,16] [1,5,10,13] [1,5,10,14]
i.e. every combination of one cell per row, not the four actual columns.

Cause: mapLowerDim (src/SizedGrid/Grid/Grid.hs:221-233) ends in

    traverse (fmap unGrid . f . Grid) (splitVectorBySize ... v)

With f = [] the list applicative is the cartesian product, so n sub-grids each
yielding n windows gives n^n results. For the real 9x9 sudoko board that is
9^9 = 387,420,489 grids -- sudoko/src/Main.hs:54 'columns' and :56 'squares' will
both hang.

Fix: the intent is a zip, not a product. Use ZipList:

    columns = getZipList $ mapLowerDim (ZipList . gridWindows) board

That yields exactly 4 (resp. 9). Worth checking 'squares' the same way -- it is
'gridWindows' then 'mapLowerDim gridWindows', so it has the same defect.

Separately, gridWindows' signature is weak:
  - 'small' and 'big' are only related by 'CoordNat big `Mod` CoordNat small ~ 0';
    nothing ties the element counts to 'rest', so a caller can ask for a shape that
    does not tile the source.
  - splitVectorBySize's final clause returns a short trailing chunk rather than
    failing, so a non-dividing size silently yields a malformed last Grid.
  - The name says 'windows' but the behaviour is non-overlapping tiles. Sliding
    windows and disjoint tiles are different operations; pick one and name it.

Suggest landing this as two functions -- 'gridTiles' (disjoint, what the code does)
and a real 'gridWindows' (overlapping, stride 1) -- with the ZipList variant for
the lower-dimension case.

title: FromJSON (Grid cs a) does not validate length, silently builds a Grid whose vector is the wrong size
description:
CONFIRMED empirically.

src/SizedGrid/Grid/Grid.hs:145-151

    instance (All IsCoordLifted cs, FromJSON a) => FromJSON (Grid cs a) where
      parseJSON v = case (shape :: Shape cs) of
        ShapeNil -> Grid . V.singleton <$> parseJSON v
        ShapeCons _ -> do
          a :: [Grid (Tail cs) a] <- parseJSON v
          return $ Grid $ foldMap unGrid a

Nothing checks that the outer list has exactly CoordNat (Head cs) elements.

Probe result:
    decode "[[1,2,3],[4,5,6]]" :: Maybe (Grid '[Ordinal 3, Ordinal 3] Int)
    => Just, with unGrid length 6 (type promises 9)

The whole point of the library is that the type pins the size. A decoded Grid that
breaks the invariant makes every downstream operation unsound:
  - index/gridIndex do 'v V.! coordPosition c' -> out-of-bounds exception at runtime
  - Applicative (<*>) is V.zipWith -> silently truncates
  - collapseGrid produces a ragged result

Contrast with gridFromList (src/SizedGrid/Grid/Grid.hs:121-132), which DOES check
'length cg == natVal (Proxy @(CoordNat (Head cs)))' and returns Nothing. FromJSON
should reuse exactly that logic.

Note the constraints are also asymmetric: ToJSON needs AllGridSizeKnown + SListI,
FromJSON needs All IsCoordLifted. FromJSON needs the KnownNat evidence to validate,
so aligning them on AllGridSizeKnown is part of the fix.

Why the test suite misses it: aesonLaws only round-trips well-formed values.
Add a negative test decoding a short/long array and asserting Nothing.

comments.author: Kevin Horlick
comments.text:
FIXED. FromJSON now validates the length at every dimension and 'fail's otherwise, so a decoded Grid always satisfies the size invariant. Constraints aligned with ToJSON (AllGridSizeKnown cs, SListI cs), which is what supplies the KnownNat evidence needed to check.

Ragged input is rejected by the recursion: the outer list length is checked at each level. All three negative tests (too few rows / too many rows / ragged rows) now pass.

title: HardWrap violates AffineSpace laws: (.-.) clamps negative differences to 0
description:
CONFIRMED empirically (GHC 9.8.4, tests/probe).

src/SizedGrid/Coord/HardWrap.hs:56-60

    HardWrap a .-. HardWrap b = max 0 $ min maxCoordSize (ordinalToNum a - ordinalToNum b)

With a=1, b=3 in HardWrap 10: (a .-. b) == 0, so b .+^ (a .-. b) == 3, not 1.
The AffineSpace law 'b .+^ (a .-. b) == a' is broken. Periodic satisfies it (control check passed).

Root cause: Diff (HardWrap n) = Integer should be a *signed displacement*, but (.-.) clamps
it into the coordinate range. Clamping belongs in (.+^) only, never in (.-.).

Downstream impact (real, observed in ../aoc):
  - moorePoints 1 at a HardWrap corner returns 9 points, only 4 distinct.
  - ../aoc/src/2025/04.hs:62 has to write 'filter (/= coord) . nubOrd . moorePoints 1'.
  - ../aoc/src/2015/18.hs and ../aoc/src/2018/18.hs abandon moorePoints entirely and
    hand-roll neighborsOf with 'toEnum nr :| toEnum nc :| EmptyCoord'.

Why the test suite misses it: tests/Test/Utils.hs:98-110 affineSpaceLaws only checks
'a .+^ zeroV == a' and 'a .-. a == zeroV'. Both hold under clamping.

Fix sketch:
  - (.-.) returns the true signed difference (no clamp).
  - (.+^) keeps clamping, OR HardWrap stops being an AffineSpace and grows a partial
    offset API returning Maybe (see the 'safe neighbour offset' issue).
  - Strengthen affineSpaceLaws with the round-trip law 'b .+^ (a .-. b) === a'.

comments.author: Kevin Horlick
comments.text:
FIXED. HardWrap's (.-.) now returns the true signed difference; the clamp stays in (.+^) alone, which is what keeps results in range.

The round-trip law 'b .+^ (a .-. b) === a' now passes for HardWrap and for the mixed Coord [HardWrap 10, Periodic 20]. Verified on GHC 9.12.3 and 9.14.1 via 'nix flake check' (exit 0, all checks passed).

WARNING, see sized-grid-7bp: this breaks ../aoc/src/2018/06.hs, which relied on the clamp to compute an absolute value ('max 0 (a-b) + max 0 (b-a) == |a-b|'). Its manhattan function now returns 0 for every pair, confirmed by probe. Must be patched in the same change set.

title: ShrinkableGrid window constraint had x and y transposed
description:
Found while fixing sized-grid-2h0, and fixed in the same change.

src/SizedGrid/Grid/Grid.hs, instance ShrinkableGrid (c x ': cs) (c y ': as) (c z ': bs)
carried the constraint:

    z <= (x - y + 1)

where x is the number of window positions, y the source size and z the window size.
The correct relation is that a window of z at any of the x offsets must fit in y:

    (x - 1) + z <= y     i.e.   x + z <= y + 1     i.e.   z <= y - x + 1

so x and y were the wrong way round.

Why it was never noticed: the only test (tests/Test/Shrink.hs) uses x == y == 3, where
both readings collapse to 'z <= 1'. The honest case of windowing a 5-grid into three
positions of 3 (x=3, y=5, z=3) was REJECTED by the old constraint: 3 - 5 truncates to 0
in Nat, giving 'z <= 1'.

FIXED: constraint restated as 'x + z <= y + 1'. Stating it as an addition rather than a
truncating Nat subtraction also keeps it in reach of the solver.

The two remaining obligations inside 'helper' (n <= y and z <= y - n, where n is the
existential offset from asSizeProxy with n + 1 <= x) follow by linear arithmetic but
mention a truncating subtraction over an existential, which GHC cannot discharge.
ghc-typelits-natnormalise was tried and did NOT help (it does not use given <= premises
to discharge wanted <= goals), and its ghc-tcplugins-extra dependency caps at GHC <9.13,
which broke the 9.14 build. So the plugins were dropped and the facts are asserted in
SizedGrid.Internal.Type.windowFits, in the same style as the existing takeAddIsId.
Soundness rests on the instance constraint, which IS checked at every call site.

FOLLOW-UP: tests/Test/Shrink.hs still only covers x == y == 3. Add a discriminating
case (x=3, y=5, z=3) that would have caught the transposition.

comments.author: Kevin Horlick
comments.text:
FIXED in the same change as sized-grid-2h0. Constraint restated as 'x + z <= y + 1'.

The follow-up named in the description is DONE: tests/Test/Shrink.hs now has the discriminating case (x=3 positions, y=5 source, z=3 window) at all three offsets, which the old transposed constraint rejected at compile time. Suite is 80 tests, all passing on GHC 9.12.3 and 9.14.1.

title: Use RequiredTypeArguments to delete Proxy from the public API
description:
GHC 9.10+ has RequiredTypeArguments ('forall n -> ...'), so the Proxy-passing style
throughout this library is now avoidable. Kevin has approved targeting 9.12/9.14
features (2026-08-09).

Current Proxy-taking API:
  - src/SizedGrid/Grid/Grid.hs:190  dropGrid  :: KnownNat n => Proxy n -> Grid '[c m] x -> Grid '[c (m - n)] x
  - src/SizedGrid/Grid/Grid.hs:197  takeGrid  :: KnownNat n => Proxy n -> Grid '[c n] x
  - src/SizedGrid/Coord/Class.hs:37 sCoordSized  :: Proxy (c n) -> Proxy n
  - src/SizedGrid/Coord/Class.hs:41 maxCoordSize :: KnownNat n => Proxy (c n) -> Integer
  - src/SizedGrid/Coord/Class.hs:45 maxCoord     :: KnownNat n => Proxy n -> c n
  - src/SizedGrid/Coord/Class.hs:48 asSizeProxy  :: c n -> (forall m. ... => Proxy m -> x) -> x

After:
    takeGrid :: forall n -> (KnownNat n, n <= m) => Grid '[c m] x -> Grid '[c n] x
    takeGrid 3 g        -- instead of takeGrid (Proxy @3) g

    maxCoordSize :: forall (c :: Nat -> Type) n -> KnownNat n => Integer

Also removes Proxy from test and user code: tests/Main.hs is full of
'Proxy @(Periodic 10)' arguments, and ../aoc passes Proxy around too.

Related modernisation to do in the same pass:
  - default-language: GHC2024 (GHC 9.10+). GHC2024 already implies DataKinds, GADTs,
    LambdaCase, MonoLocalBinds, DerivingStrategies, RoleAnnotations,
    ExplicitNamespaces, DisambiguateRecordFields on top of GHC2021's
    ScopedTypeVariables/TypeApplications/TypeOperators/FlexibleContexts/RankNTypes.
    That deletes most of the 10-20 line LANGUAGE headers on every module.
  - TypeAbstractions ('instance ... where method @a = ...') for the IsCoord instances
    that currently need InstanceSigs + ScopedTypeVariables to bind the type variable.
  - OrPatterns (GHC 9.12) where the coord classes match several constructors alike.
  - DerivingStrategies to make the many 'deriving instance' lines in
    Coord/Periodic.hs:37-42 and Coord/HardWrap.hs:30-36 explicit about newtype vs
    stock vs anyclass.

Sequence after the plugin adoption (sized-grid-h56) so the constraint changes and the
signature changes land together rather than touching every signature twice.

title: Establish a property-test baseline that would have caught the confirmed bugs
description:
The existing suite passes 62 tests while three genuine bugs sit in the library. The
laws being tested are too weak.

Gaps found:
  - tests/Test/Utils.hs:98-110 affineSpaceLaws tests only 'a .+^ zeroV == a' and
    'a .-. a == zeroV'. Both hold under HardWrap's clamping. Add the round-trip law
    'b .+^ (a .-. b) === a' -- it fails on HardWrap today.
  - aesonLaws (tests/Test/Utils.hs:41-48) only round-trips valid values. Add negative
    cases: decoding a too-short / too-long array must be Nothing.
  - No test asserts the core invariant 'V.length (unGrid g) == MaxCoordSize cs'.
    Make it a property over every Grid-producing operation: tabulate, gridFromList,
    takeGrid, dropGrid, splitHigherDim, combineHigherDim, shrinkGrid, mapLowerDim,
    fmap, <*>, and FromJSON. takeGrid and splitHigherDim fail it today.
  - No Comonad law tests for FocusedGrid (extract . duplicate == id, etc.).
  - No Representable law test (tabulate . index == id) beyond the 2D case in
    tests/Main.hs:81-82.
  - No Distributive law test.
  - shrinkGrid has exactly one example-based test (tests/Test/Shrink.hs) and no
    properties.

Also: tests/Main.hs:34-38 defines Arbitrary via 'oneof (map pure [minBound .. maxBound])',
which builds the entire domain for each sample -- fine at size 10, quadratic at 300.

Write these BEFORE fixing the bugs, so each fix has a failing test to turn green.

comments.author: Kevin Horlick
comments.text:
Baseline is in and RED in exactly the predicted places: 7 of 78 tests fail.

New: tests/Test/Invariant.hs (size invariant + negative JSON + take/split), and the round-trip law 'b .+^ (a .-. b) === a' added to affineSpaceLaws in tests/Test/Utils.hs.

Failing, each mapping to a filed defect:
  - HardWrap: b .+^ (a .-. b) == a            -> sized-grid-0kf
  - Coord [HardWrap 10, Periodic 20]: same    -> sized-grid-0kf
  - JSON too few rows / too many rows / ragged -> sized-grid-miz
  - takeGrid @9 of a 3-grid: expected 9, got 3 -> sized-grid-2h0
  - splitHigherDim dishonest annotation: expected 21, got 6 -> sized-grid-2h0

Discriminating correctly: Periodic passes the affine round-trip, and all five well-formed-construction cases (gridFromList, tabulate, pure, fmap, encode/decode round trip) pass. So the law is right and only HardWrap violates it.

NOTE: 'nix flake check' is red until wave 02 lands, by design.

Still open: Comonad laws for FocusedGrid, Representable/Distributive laws, shrinkGrid properties, and the O(n^2) Arbitrary in tests/Main.hs:34-38.

comments.author: Kevin Horlick
comments.text:
DONE for its blocking purpose. Every defect this issue gated had a failing test written first, and all are now green:

  - HardWrap / mixed-Coord affine round trip  -> sized-grid-0kf, fixed
  - JSON too few / too many / ragged rows     -> sized-grid-miz, fixed
  - takeGrid @9, splitHigherDim remainder     -> sized-grid-2h0, fixed (now compile errors)

The baseline also did its job beyond the predicted set: tightening the take/split signatures exposed a fourth defect, the transposed ShrinkableGrid constraint (sized-grid-px9), which the x == y == 3 test could not distinguish.

Suite went 78 tests / 7 failing -> 80 tests / 0 failing. Two runtime cases became compile-time rejections (harness filed as sized-grid-cti), and four new cases were added: dropGrid sizing plus three discriminating shrink windows.

Verified green on GHC 9.12.3 AND 9.14.1 via 'nix flake check' (exit 0, all checks passed).

Remaining test-coverage work split out to sized-grid-ryy so this can close.

title: No benchmarks; performance work is currently unmeasurable
description:
There is no benchmark suite, so every performance claim about this library
(Ordinal representation, allCoord caching, unboxed vectors) is speculation.

Add a criterion (or tasty-bench) suite covering the operations the real workloads hit:

  - index / gridIndex on Grid '[HardWrap 300, HardWrap 300] Int
    (the shape ../aoc/src/2018/11.hs uses)
  - tabulate at the same size
  - imap / ifoldMap' / itraverse -- these rebuild allCoord every call
  - the comonadic step: extend over a FocusedGrid, as in ../aoc/src/2015/18.hs
    and ../aoc/src/2018/18.hs and gameOfLife/
  - coordinate arithmetic in isolation: (.+^), (.-.), toEnum, fromEnum
  - allCoord itself
  - collapseGrid / gridFromList round-trip
  - JSON encode/decode

Record a baseline on GHC 9.12 BEFORE touching the Ordinal representation, so the
refactor can be judged. tasty-bench is the lighter dependency and integrates with the
existing tasty suite.

This gates the Ordinal-newtype issue and the unboxed-Grid issue -- do it first.

title: Missing API: safe neighbour offset. Users emulate it with strengthenCoord/weakenCoord through a larger grid
description:
The most-wanted operation on a bounded grid is 'move by a delta, or fail if that leaves
the grid'. The library has no such function, so users build it out of parts.

../aoc/src/2024/04.hs:63-80 -- to walk three steps in a direction on an n x n grid the
user has to widen the coordinate type to n+1, offset there, then narrow back:

    i, j, k :: Coord '[Periodic (n + 1), Periodic (n + 1)]
    i = strengthenCoord c .+^ d
    j = i .+^ d
    k = j .+^ d
    ... mapMaybe (traverse weakenCoord) ...
        \\ plusNat @n @1 \\ leTrans @1 @n @(n + 1) \\ plusMonotone2 @n @0 @1

That is a lot of machinery to express 'neighbour, or Nothing'. It also only works
because Periodic's wrap-around at n+1 happens not to collide for small deltas -- it is
not actually a bounds check.

../aoc/src/2015/18.hs:64-66 and ../aoc/src/2018/18.hs:78-80 give up on the library
entirely and hand-roll:

    neighborsOf = [ toEnum nr :| toEnum nc :| EmptyCoord | ... ]

../aoc/src/2025/04.hs:62 uses moorePoints but must repair the result:

    experiment (filter (/= coord) . nubOrd . moorePoints 1) g

Proposed API:

    -- fails instead of clamping or wrapping
    offsetCoord  :: Coord cs -> Diff (Coord cs) -> Maybe (Coord cs)
    neighbours   :: Coord cs -> [Coord cs]   -- Moore, excludes centre, no duplicates
    neighbours4  :: Coord cs -> [Coord cs]   -- von Neumann, excludes centre

with the boundary behaviour driven by the coord type rather than by clamping:
Periodic wraps (total), and a new 'Bounded'/'Clipped' coord returns Nothing at the
edge. Note moorePoints/vonNeumanPoints currently INCLUDE the centre, which every
observed caller then filters out -- the default is wrong.

Blocked on the HardWrap AffineSpace fix, since that is what makes the current
neighbour story incorrect.

comments.author: Kevin Horlick
comments.text:
Empirical check of the moorePoints half of sized-grid-7bp: the nubOrd workarounds at
../aoc/src/2025/04.hs:62 (and the commented-out ones in 2015/18 and 2018/18) must STAY.
The 0kf fix did not help them.

0kf only desugared (.-.); HardWrap's (.+^) still clamps
(src/SizedGrid/Coord/HardWrap.hs:62-65), and moorePoints is built out of (.+^)
(src/SizedGrid/Coord.hs:250-257), so every off-grid offset folds back onto the edge
cell. Measured on HardWrap 5 x HardWrap 5:

    moorePoints 1 (0,0) -> 9 results, 4 distinct   <- 5 duplicates
    moorePoints 1 (2,2) -> 9 results, 9 distinct

This is the concrete argument for the 'no duplicates' clause in the proposed
'neighbours' API above: dedup cannot be the caller's job when the clamp is what
created the duplicates.

Note vonNeumanPoints (src/SizedGrid/Coord.hs:275-284) was silently repaired by 0kf:
its 'min (new .-. c) (c .-. new)' picked the componentwise minimum of the two signed
diffs, which under the old clamp was 0 for every pair, so the radius filter passed
everything. It now yields -|d| and the abs makes the filter real. It still inherits the
duplicate cells from moorePoints.

title: Modernise sized-grid.cabal: cabal-version 1.10, zero version bounds, missing modules, per-file LANGUAGE noise
description:
Current sized-grid.cabal problems:

  - 'cabal-version: >=1.10' (line 3). Modern baseline is 'cabal-version: 2.4' or 3.0,
    which unlocks common stanzas and the modern module syntax.
  - Library build-depends has NO version bounds at all: 'base,' 'aeson ,' 'lens ,' etc.
    Unacceptable for a Hackage release; also means nothing pins the library away from
    a breaking aeson/lens major bump.
  - SizedGrid.Internal.Type is in neither exposed-modules nor other-modules.
  - Every module repeats 10-20 LANGUAGE pragmas. GHC2021 (default on GHC 9.2+) already
    implies ScopedTypeVariables, TypeApplications, TypeOperators, FlexibleContexts,
    FlexibleInstances, RankNTypes, StandaloneDeriving, GADTs and more. Setting
    'default-language: GHC2021' plus a short 'default-extensions: DataKinds,
    TypeFamilies, UndecidableInstances, PolyKinds' would delete most of the headers.
  - The CPP '#if MIN_VERSION_base(4,11,0)' blocks in SizedGrid/Coord/Periodic.hs:25-28,
    SizedGrid/Grid/Class.hs:19-22 and tests/Test/Utils.hs:16-19 exist to support
    base < 4.11 (GHC 8.2). Dead now; delete the CPP and the pragma.
  - src/SizedGrid/Grid/Grid.hs:1 sets '-Wno-redundant-constraints' for the whole module,
    which hides real problems (e.g. the Monoid/Semigroup constraints on the Comonad
    instance in SizedGrid/Grid/Focused.hs:26-32 look unnecessary). Remove the blanket
    suppression and fix or annotate the individual cases.
  - The 'readme' test-suite is commented out (lines 74-89), so README.lhs is never
    compiled and the tutorial can silently rot.
  - Consider hpack (package.yaml) for consistency with ../aoc, which already uses it.

Note the version is 0.2.0.2 but ChangeLog.md still says '0.2.0.0 -- NOT PUBLISHED'.
close_reason: CPP stripped from all three modules, -Widentities warnings fixed (build is now warning-clean), README.lhs test-suite re-enabled via markdown-unlit and made to actually run a glider rather than 'main = return ()'. hpack decided against, rationale in comments. -Wno-redundant-constraints left to sized-grid-cpw where the underlying fix lives. Verified on ghc 9.12.3 and 9.14.1 via nix, both suites green.

comments.author: Kevin Horlick
comments.text:
Landed: cabal-version 3.0, default-language GHC2024 via a 'common lang' stanza, real version bounds on every dependency, SizedGrid.Internal.Type listed in other-modules, tested-with 9.8.4/9.10.1/9.12.3/9.14.1, bytestring added for the new test module.

Verified on BOTH compilers: 'nix build .#sized-grid' (ghc912, 9.12.3) and the ghc914 output (9.14.1) each compile the library and run the suite. GHC2024 needed no module-header changes.

Still open in this issue: strip the now-dead CPP blocks (Periodic.hs:25-28, Grid/Class.hs:19-22, Test/Utils.hs:16-19), remove the blanket -Wno-redundant-constraints in Grid/Grid.hs:1, re-enable the README.lhs test-suite, and decide on hpack.

comments.author: Kevin Horlick
comments.text:
Second pass, remaining items closed out.

CPP removed. base is pinned >=4.19 in sized-grid.cabal:66, so MIN_VERSION_base(4,11,0)
is unconditionally true and all three '#else import Data.Semigroup' arms were dead.

title: Adopt ghc-typelits-natnormalise and ghc-typelits-knownnat to remove manual Nat proof plumbing
description:
The library currently discharges type-level arithmetic by hand with Data.Constraint.Nat
and, in places, unsafeCoerce.

Manual plumbing in the library:
  - src/SizedGrid/Ordinal.hs:61  '\\ plusNat @n @1'
  - src/SizedGrid/Ordinal.hs:68  '\\ leTrans @(x + 1) @n @m'
  - src/SizedGrid/Ordinal.hs:79  '\\ plusMinusInverse3 @1 @m \\ minusNat @m @1'
  - src/SizedGrid/Coord.hs:294-305  the whole AllSizedKnown class exists only to
    thread 'KnownNat (MaxCoordSize cs)' through timesNat

And it leaks all the way into user code. ../aoc/src/2024/04.hs:78-80 has to write:

    \\ plusNat @n @1
    \\ leTrans @1 @n @(n + 1)
    \\ plusMonotone2 @n @0 @1

and ../aoc/src/2024/04.hs:96-97 the same again via withDict. That is the library's
proof obligations showing up in a puzzle solution.

../aoc already depends on ghc-typelits-natnormalise and ghc-typelits-knownnat.
sized-grid does not. Adding

    ghc-options: -fplugin=GHC.TypeLits.Normalise -fplugin=GHC.TypeLits.KnownNat.Solver

discharges most 'KnownNat (n * m)', 'n <= n + 1' and 'n + 1 <= m' goals automatically.

Expected wins:
  - AllSizedKnown (src/SizedGrid/Coord.hs:294-305) likely disappears entirely, which
    simplifies the constraint on nearly every Grid function.
  - Callers stop needing KnownNat (n * n) in signatures -- cf. ../aoc/src/2025/04.hs:33
    'parse :: (KnownNat n, KnownNat (n GHC.* n)) => ...'
  - The unsound axioms in SizedGrid/Internal/Type.hs become unnecessary.

Caveat: plugins are a build-time dependency for *users* too if the constraints appear
in exported signatures. Measure how much of the public API simplifies before
committing. Do this before the Ordinal representation change -- it will make that
refactor much less painful.

comments.author: Kevin Horlick
comments.text:
EVIDENCE AGAINST, from trying it during the wave-02 fixes (sized-grid-2h0 / sized-grid-px9).

Both plugins were added and then REMOVED again:

1. They did not solve the problem. The wanted was 'z <= y - n' from a given 'n + 1 <= x' plus 'x + z <= y + 1'. ghc-typelits-natnormalise does not use given <= premises to discharge wanted <= goals, so the error was unchanged ('Cannot satisfy: z <= y - m'). ghc-typelits-presburger is the plugin that does this, and it is marked BROKEN in nixpkgs.

2. They break GHC 9.14. ghc-typelits-natnormalise depends on ghc-tcplugins-extra, whose bound is 'ghc >=7.10 && <9.13'; with GHC 9.14.1 the nix build fails at configure with [Cabal-8010]. Since the flake checks both 9.12.3 and 9.14.1, adopting them would have cost 9.14 support outright.

What worked instead: restate constraints as additions rather than truncating Nat subtractions where possible ('x + z <= y + 1' not 'z <= y - x + 1'), and assert the residual existential facts in SizedGrid.Internal.Type.windowFits, in the same style as the pre-existing takeAddIsId.

Recommend this issue be reconsidered or closed unless presburger becomes usable AND ghc-tcplugins-extra gains a 9.14 bound. Retest before adopting.

comments.author: Kevin Horlick
comments.text:
RETESTED 2026-08-09 as the previous comment asked. Both blockers still stand, and one
of them is worse than 'nixpkgs has not caught up'.

1. ghc-tcplugins-extra has NO GHC 9.14 release at all -- this is upstream, not a pin
   problem. Hackage's version list tops out at 0.5, whose bound is literally
   'ghc >=7.10 && <9.13', and whose tested-with stops at GHC 9.12.1. Reproduced the
   failure end to end by building the plugin against the 9.14 package set:

       Configuring ghc-tcplugins-extra-0.5...
       Error: [Cabal-8010]
       Encountered missing or private dependencies:
           ghc >=7.10 && <9.13 (installed: 9.14.1)

   ghc-typelits-natnormalise 0.7.12 and ghc-typelits-knownnat 0.7.13 both sit on top of
   it, so all three are unavailable on 9.14 together.

2. ghc-typelits-presburger 0.7.4.2 is still meta.broken = true in nixpkgs for both
   ghc912 and ghc914. It remains the only plugin that would discharge the actual wanted
   from the wave-02 work (a '<=' goal from '<=' givens); natnormalise does not do that.

Not a stale-pin excuse: flake.lock's nixpkgs is 2026-08-06, three days old.

Also ruling out the obvious workaround, so nobody spends time on it: adopting the
plugins only for GHC < 9.13 via 'if impl(ghc < 9.13)' in the cabal file does not work
for this library. The plugins do not simplify signatures by themselves -- they let us
WRITE simpler ones. Any signature written to depend on them would then fail to compile
on 9.14, so the public API would differ by compiler. That is not acceptable for a
library, and API simplification is the entire point of this issue.

Deferring rather than closing: the plan is sound the moment upstream moves. RETEST
CONDITION, both must hold:
  - a ghc-tcplugins-extra release accepting ghc >= 9.14 (check Hackage, not just
    nixpkgs), and
  - ghc-typelits-presburger no longer marked broken in nixpkgs.
Until then sized-grid-qh9 should proceed on its own option 2.

title: sudoko/gameOfLife/ising-example do not build: ancient resolvers and base <4.13 bounds

title: Grid is a leaky abstraction: constructor and unGrid are exported, no smart constructor
description:
src/SizedGrid/Grid/Grid.hs:40-42

    newtype Grid (cs :: [Type]) a = Grid { unGrid :: V.Vector a }
      deriving (Eq, Show, Functor, Foldable, Traversable, Eq1, Show1, GHC.Generic)

Both Grid and unGrid are exported (the module has no export list at all -- every
module in the library uses an implicit 'module M where'). Anyone can build a Grid
whose vector length disagrees with MaxCoordSize cs, which is the one invariant the
library exists to enforce. The FromJSON bug and the takeGrid bug are both instances
of this.

Evidence users reach through it: ../aoc/src/2018/11.hs:31
    prefixSum1D = Grid . V.scanl1' (+) . unGrid
That is a legitimate need (prefix sums along an axis) with no API for it, so the
user bypasses the abstraction. Length-preserving uses like this are fine -- the
point is the type does not distinguish them from unsound ones.

Proposal:
  - Give every module an explicit export list.
  - Export the Grid type but not the constructor from SizedGrid.Grid.Grid.
  - Add SizedGrid.Grid.Unsafe exposing UnsafeGrid/unGrid for the escape hatch,
    documented as 'you must preserve length'.
  - Add a safe 'gridFromVector :: ... => V.Vector a -> Maybe (Grid cs a)'.
  - Add the length-preserving combinators people actually want, so the escape hatch
    is rarely needed: mapAxis / scanAxis / prefix sums along a dimension
    (covers the ../aoc/src/2018/11.hs summed-area-table use directly).

Explicit export lists also let -Wmissing-export-lists be turned on, which ../aoc
already enables for its own code.

title: Ordinal's GADT representation costs a KnownNat dictionary + someNatVal allocation per arithmetic op
description:
The central performance problem.

src/SizedGrid/Ordinal.hs:31-32

    data Ordinal m where
      Ordinal :: (KnownNat n, KnownNat m, n + 1 <= m) => Proxy n -> Ordinal m

Every Ordinal value carries a type-level Nat and its dictionary. Consequences:

  - ordinalToNum goes Proxy -> natVal -> Integer -> fromIntegral. Integer, not Int.
  - numToOrdinal (src/SizedGrid/Ordinal.hs:50-61) calls someNatVal (allocates a
    SomeNat, builds a KnownNat dictionary via unsafeCoerce) plus cmpNat, on EVERY
    construction.
  - toEnum = fromJust . numToOrdinal, so enumerating an axis allocates one Nat
    dictionary per element.
  - Periodic's (<>), negateV, (.+^), (.-.) and HardWrap's equivalents all round-trip
    through numToOrdinal. A single coordinate addition allocates a type-level natural.

Observed cost in practice: ../aoc/src/2018/11.hs works on Grid '[HardWrap 300, HardWrap 300]
and iterates 'allCoord' (90,000 coords), each one an NP of two GADTs carrying dictionaries.

Proposal: make it a newtype over Int with a smart constructor.

    newtype Ordinal (m :: Nat) = UnsafeOrdinal { ordinalToInt :: Int }

The only thing the GADT buys at runtime is asSizeProxy (src/SizedGrid/Coord/Class.hs:48-53),
which recovers 'Proxy m' with 'm + 1 <= n'. That is used in exactly one place
(shrinkGrid, src/SizedGrid/Grid/Grid.hs:248-254). Reconstruct the evidence there via
someNatVal at that single call site instead of paying for it on every value.

Expected: coordinate arithmetic becomes machine-word Int ops; Ordinal becomes
unboxable, which unblocks the unboxed-Grid work.

Do this behind the existing _Ordinal prism / numToOrdinal / ordinalToNum API so
most call sites are unaffected. Benchmark first (see the criterion issue).

comments.author: Kevin Horlick
comments.text:
Dependency on sized-grid-h56 removed. h56 was retested on 2026-08-09 and deferred --

title: allCoord is rebuilt from scratch on every imap/ifoldMap/itraverse/tabulate
description:
src/SizedGrid/Grid/Grid.hs:67-75

    imap func (Grid v)      = Grid $ V.zipWith func (V.fromList allCoord) v
    ifoldMap func (Grid v)  = foldMap id $ V.zipWith func (V.fromList allCoord) v
    itraverse func (Grid v) = Grid <$> sequenceA (V.zipWith func (V.fromList allCoord) v)

and src/SizedGrid/Grid/Grid.hs:64

    tabulate func = Grid $ V.fromList $ map func allCoord

'allCoord' (src/SizedGrid/Coord.hs:206-212) builds the full coordinate list through
the list monad over an NP, then V.fromList copies it into a vector. This happens on
every single indexed traversal, and each element is a heap-allocated NP I cs whose
components each carry a KnownNat dictionary.

For Grid '[HardWrap 300, HardWrap 300] that is 90,000 NP allocations per imap.

Also src/SizedGrid/Coord.hs:220-237: coordPosition recomputes the per-axis size
product ('sizeOfList') on every call, in Integer, and index calls coordPosition for
every access.

Options, roughly in order of payoff:
  1. Cache the coordinate vector per type in a CAF: 'allCoordVector :: V.Vector (Coord cs)'
     bound at top level so GHC shares it across calls. Needs care to actually float.
  2. Precompute the axis strides once (a small [Int]) rather than folding sizes each
     time in coordPosition.
  3. Better: make imap/ifoldMap/itraverse iterate positions as Int and only
     materialise a Coord when the user function demands one. Most callers use
     fromEnum on the result anyway -- see ../aoc/src/2018/11.hs:40
     '(fromEnum -> r) :| (fromEnum -> c) :| _'.

Depends on the Ordinal representation change for the biggest win.

title: takeGrid and splitHigherDim have unsound type signatures (no n <= m; z unconstrained)
description:
CONFIRMED empirically.

1) takeGrid -- src/SizedGrid/Grid/Grid.hs:197-198

    takeGrid :: KnownNat n => Proxy n -> Grid '[c m] x -> Grid '[c n] x
    takeGrid p (Grid v) = Grid $ V.take (fromIntegral $ natVal p) v

Missing 'n <= m'. Probe:
    takeGrid (Proxy @9) (gridFromList [1,2,3] :: Grid '[Ordinal 3] Int) :: Grid '[Ordinal 9] Int
    => unGrid length 3, while the type claims 9. Invariant broken, silently.

2) splitHigherDim -- src/SizedGrid/Grid/Grid.hs:200-219

    splitHigherDim :: forall c as x y z a. (KnownNat x, KnownNat y, y <= x, ...)
      => Grid (c x ': as) a -> (Grid (c y ': as) a, Grid (c z ': as) a)

'z' is a completely free type variable in the result. The caller picks any z they
like and the second component's type is a lie unless they happen to pick x - y.
tests/Main.hs:136-138 only passes because it annotates z correctly by hand.

3) dropGrid -- src/SizedGrid/Grid/Grid.hs:190-195 has the same shape of problem;
   'm - n' is stuck rather than checked when n > m.

Fix: add 'n <= m' to takeGrid/dropGrid and fix splitHigherDim's result to
'Grid (c (x - y) ': as) a'. This is a breaking API change but restores the
core guarantee the library exists to provide.

Related: this class of hole is exactly what ghc-typelits-natnormalise +
ghc-typelits-knownnat make cheap to state and discharge.

comments.author: Kevin Horlick
comments.text:
FIXED. takeGrid and dropGrid now require 'n <= m'; splitHigherDim's remainder is 'c (x - y)' instead of a free variable.

The stricter signatures immediately caught a fourth bug: ShrinkableGrid's window constraint had x and y transposed. Filed and fixed as sized-grid-px9.

Consequence for the tests: the two cases that used to fail at RUNTIME are now compile errors ('Cannot satisfy: 9 <= 3'), so they cannot be runtime assertions any more. They are documented in tests/Test/Invariant.hs and a compile-fail harness is filed as sized-grid-cti. The positive half (sizes promised == sizes held) is still asserted.

No impact on ../aoc: it uses none of takeGrid/dropGrid/splitHigherDim/shrinkGrid.

title: fromJust in Ordinal construction: seven call sites total only by an unchecked invariant
description:
Split out of sized-grid-0vq part (b); part (a), the four unreachable 'error' calls, is done.

'fromJust . numToOrdinal' appears in arithmetic that is total only because a mod or a
clamp happened just beforehand, which nothing checks:

  - src/SizedGrid/Coord/Periodic.hs:42, 54, 65, 74
  - src/SizedGrid/Coord/HardWrap.hs:44, 61
  - src/SizedGrid/Ordinal.hs:82        toEnum = fromJust . numToOrdinal
  - src/SizedGrid/Coord/Class.hs:83    maxCoord

Each is correct today, but the invariant lives in the reader's head, and every one of
them turns a future off-by-one into 'Maybe.fromJust: Nothing' with no indication of
which coordinate or which operation produced it.

This is deliberately NOT fixed by sprinkling error messages on the existing code. The
right fix arrives with sized-grid-upo: once Ordinal is a newtype over Int, all of these
collapse into a single 'unsafeOrdinalFromInt' whose precondition is stated once, checked
with an assert in a debug build, and free in a release build. Doing it before upo means
writing the same defensive code twice.
acceptance_criteria: No fromJust remains in src/; the single unchecked construction point documents its precondition and is assert-checked when compiled with -fno-ignore-asserts.

title: AllGridSizeKnown is a type family, so KnownNat (n*n) leaks into every consumer signature
description:
Split out of sized-grid-cpw bullet 4, with the mechanism now identified.

The library has two ways of saying 'the sizes are known' and they behave very
differently for users:

  - AllSizedKnown (src/SizedGrid/Coord.hs:294-302) is a CLASS whose instance chain is
    '(KnownNat n, AllSizedKnown as) => AllSizedKnown (c n ': as)'. GHC discharges it by
    instance resolution from 'KnownNat n' alone, and the total-size fact is handed back
    at the value level as 'sizeProof :: Dict (KnownNat (MaxCoordSize cs))'. Callers pay
    nothing: ../aoc/src/2015/18.hs:38 gets Comonad on a FocusedGrid with only
    '(KnownNat n, 1 <= n)'.

  - AllGridSizeKnown (src/SizedGrid/Grid/Grid.hs:92-97) is a TYPE FAMILY that expands to
    a conjunction of KnownNat constraints, including 'KnownNat (MaxCoordSize cs)'. A type
    family cannot be discharged by instance resolution, so the whole expansion lands in
    the user's context.

That is the direct cause of the impact measured in cpw:

    ../aoc/src/2025/04.hs:33  parse :: (KnownNat n, KnownNat (n GHC.* n)) => ...
    ../aoc/src/2015/18.hs:31  parse :: (KnownNat n, KnownNat (n GHC.* n)) => ...

Both signatures carry 'KnownNat (n * n)' purely because gridFromList is constrained by
AllGridSizeKnown rather than by AllSizedKnown. Compare the FocusedGrid signatures a few
lines below in the same files, which need nothing of the sort.

Affected API: collapseGrid, gridFromList, and the ToJSON/FromJSON instances for Grid
(Grid.hs:109, :123, :135, :153).

TWO POSSIBLE FIXES, and they should be evaluated in this order:

1. Do sized-grid-h56 first. ghc-typelits-knownnat derives 'KnownNat (n * m)' from
   'KnownNat n, KnownNat m' automatically, which makes the leaked constraint solvable
   at the call site and may make this issue disappear without touching the API.

2. If it does not, convert AllGridSizeKnown from a type family to a class in the shape
   of AllSizedKnown. The obstacle is that the four call sites recurse structurally over
   'Shape cs', and from a dictionary for 'AllGridSizeKnown (x ': xs)' there is no way to
   recover 'AllGridSizeKnown xs' -- a class dictionary cannot be run backwards through
   its own instance context. So the class would need to carry the tail's evidence
   explicitly, e.g. a method returning 'Dict (AllGridSizeKnown (Tail cs))' alongside the
   KnownNat proof. Note 'All IsCoordLifted cs' already supplies
   'KnownNat (CoordNat (Head cs))' via IsCoordLifted's superclasses, so only the
   MaxCoordSize half actually needs new machinery.
design: Prefer waiting on sized-grid-h56: a plugin fix costs one cabal line and no API churn, while the class conversion changes four exported signatures and needs new Dict plumbing. Only take option 2 if the plugins are rejected or turn out not to discharge KnownNat (MaxCoordSize cs).
acceptance_criteria: ../aoc/src/2025/04.hs and ../aoc/src/2015/18.hs can drop 'KnownNat (n GHC.* n)' from their parse signatures and still compile.

comments.author: Kevin Horlick
comments.text:
Dependency on sized-grid-h56 REMOVED and option 1 is off the table for now. h56 was

Hackage at all (0.5 is capped at 'ghc < 9.13'), so natnormalise and knownnat cannot be

title: Remaining property-test gaps: Comonad/Representable/Distributive laws and O(n^2) Arbitrary
description:
Split out of sized-grid-6jd so the baseline issue can close. The baseline's blocking purpose -- write failing tests before the fixes -- is done: the three defects it gated (sized-grid-0kf, sized-grid-miz, sized-grid-2h0) each had a red test first and are now green.

Still outstanding from the original gap analysis:

  - No Comonad law tests for FocusedGrid (extract . duplicate == id,
    fmap extract . duplicate == id, duplicate . duplicate == fmap duplicate . duplicate).
  - No Representable law test (tabulate . index == id) beyond the 2D case in
    tests/Main.hs:81-82.
  - No Distributive law test.
  - shrinkGrid now has four example-based tests (tests/Test/Shrink.hs) but still no
    properties -- e.g. 'shrinkGrid at offset n == the n-th window' over arbitrary
    offsets and sizes.
  - tests/Main.hs:34-38 defines Arbitrary via 'oneof (map pure [minBound .. maxBound])',
    which builds the entire domain for each sample: fine at size 10, quadratic at 300.
    Replace with a bounded 'chooseInt' + numToOrdinal.

Also worth adding now that the size invariant is enforced: extend the Test.Invariant
size property to the operations it does not yet cover (combineHigherDim, mapLowerDim,
splitGrid/combineGrid, gridWindows).

title: Add a compile-fail test harness for the size invariants
description:
Wave 02 (sized-grid-2h0) tightened takeGrid/dropGrid/splitHigherDim so that misuse is a type error rather than a silently wrong Grid. That is the right outcome, but it means the regression tests for it cannot live in the tasty suite: 'takeGrid (Proxy @9)' of a 3-grid no longer compiles, so it cannot be asserted at runtime.

Right now those cases survive only as comments in tests/Test/Invariant.hs. Nothing would catch a future loosening of the signatures.

Options:
  - 'should-not-typecheck' (uses deferred type errors; brittle)
  - a cabal 'build-type: Custom' / shell script compiling snippets and asserting failure
  - GHC's own '-fdefer-type-errors' plus a runtime catch of TypeError
  - doctest with ':t' expectations

Cases to cover:
  - takeGrid (Proxy @9) :: Grid '[Ordinal 3] -> Grid '[Ordinal 9]   (needs 9 <= 3)
  - dropGrid (Proxy @9) on a 3-grid
  - splitHigherDim remainder annotated as anything other than x - y
  - ShrinkableGrid with a window that does not fit (x + z > y + 1)

title: Constraint hygiene: redundant superclass constraints leak into every user signature
description:
Several instances demand more than they use, and the noise propagates to callers.

  - src/SizedGrid/Grid/Focused.hs:26-32 and :36-42
    Comonad and ComonadStore for FocusedGrid both require 'All Monoid cs, All Semigroup cs'.
    The bodies only use index and tabulate, which need AllSizedKnown + All IsCoordLifted.
    The Monoid/Semigroup constraints appear unnecessary -- verify and drop them.

  - src/SizedGrid/Coord.hs:70
        instance (All Eq cs, All Ord cs) => Ord (Coord cs)
    Eq is a superclass of Ord, but 'All' does not propagate superclasses, so callers
    must write both. Fixable with a Dict-based entailment helper.

  - src/SizedGrid/Grid/Grid.hs:1 sets -Wno-redundant-constraints for the entire module,
    which is why these are not already flagged. Remove the blanket flag; the whole
    point of -Wredundant-constraints (already in ghc-options) is to catch this.

  - AllSizedKnown vs AllGridSizeKnown vs All IsCoordLifted are three overlapping ways
    of saying 'the sizes are known'. ToJSON (Grid) uses AllGridSizeKnown + SListI while
    FromJSON (Grid) uses All IsCoordLifted, for what should be dual operations.
    Consolidate to one constraint synonym.

Measured impact on users: ../aoc/src/2025/04.hs:33 and ../aoc/src/2015/18.hs:31 both
have to carry 'KnownNat (n GHC.* n)' in signatures purely to satisfy AllSizedKnown.
The typelits-plugin issue would remove most of this; this issue covers what remains.
close_reason: Focused.hs Comonad/ComonadStore shed All Monoid/All Semigroup; blanket -Wno-redundant-constraints removed from Grid/Grid.hs with two dead constraints deleted and four soundness constraints kept behind a new 'requiring' helper so the warning stays on. Ord (Coord cs) proved unfixable (GHC cannot induct over AllF for a type variable) and is now documented in place. Constraint consolidation split out as sized-grid-qh9, blocked on h56. Verified on ghc 9.12.3 and 9.14.1.

comments.author: Kevin Horlick
comments.text:
Worked through all four bullets. Two fixed, one proved impossible, one split out.

BULLET 1 -- Focused.hs Comonad/ComonadStore. FIXED. 'All Monoid cs, All Semigroup cs'
were unnecessary on both instances, exactly as suspected: the bodies only use index and
tabulate, which need nothing beyond Grid's Representable instance. Dropped from both;
library, both test suites and both nix GHCs still build. This was the worst of the four
because Comonad is the only reason to reach for a FocusedGrid at all, so every consumer
was repeating the noise.

BULLET 3 -- the blanket -Wno-redundant-constraints on Grid/Grid.hs:1. FIXED, flag gone.
With it removed GHC reported five constraints, and they split two ways:

  Genuinely dead, removed:
    combineHigherDim  IsCoord c
    splitHigherDim    IsCoord c, KnownNat x
  IsCoord buys nothing here -- a coord's size comes from CoordNat on the IsCoordLifted
  instance, not from IsCoord, so the class could not have justified the n + m or x - y
  in those result types even in principle.

  Load-bearing, KEPT:
    dropGrid/takeGrid  n <= m
    splitHigherDim     y <= x
    gridWindows        Mod (CoordNat big) (CoordNat small) ~ 0
  These are the soundness constraints added in 7bdd829. -Wredundant-constraints only
  looks at whether the BODY uses a constraint, and these are consumed by the caller's
  types, so it flags them wrongly. Drop 'y <= x' from splitHigherDim, for instance, and
  splitting a 5-grid at 9 returns a first component typed 'c 9' holding 5 elements.

  To keep the warning switched on rather than trading one blanket suppression for
  another, those four now name what they are enforcing via a new internal helper,
  SizedGrid.Internal.Type.requiring:

      takeGrid p (Grid v) = requiring @(n <= m) $ Grid $ V.take (natVal p) v

  It is 'id' with a constraint, so it is free at runtime, and it turns an invisible
  contract into a visible one. (Its body has to build a Dict rather than being plain
  'id', or the helper's own constraint gets reported as redundant.) Note it is NOT
  named 'contract' -- Data.Constraint already exports that and Grid.hs imports it.

BULLET 2 -- 'instance (All Eq cs, All Ord cs) => Ord (Coord cs)'. NOT FIXABLE. The
issue proposes a Dict-based entailment helper; that does not work here. Tried it, GHC
9.12.3 says:

    Could not deduce 'AllF Eq cs' arising from a superclass required to satisfy
    'All Eq cs', arising from the superclasses of an instance declaration
    from the context: All Ord cs

'All c cs' expands to the type family 'AllF c cs', and reducing 'AllF Eq cs' from
'AllF Ord cs' needs induction over cs, which the solver will not do for a type variable
-- it works only for concrete lists. Data.SOP.Dict.mapAll can produce the evidence, but
as a VALUE, and superclass evidence for an instance must be discharged at declaration
time where no value is in scope. Both constraints stay; the instance now carries a
comment saying why, so nobody retries this.

BULLET 4 -- consolidating AllSizedKnown / AllGridSizeKnown / All IsCoordLifted. SPLIT
OUT as sized-grid-qh9, blocked on sized-grid-h56.

  First, part of this bullet is stale: ToJSON and FromJSON for Grid are already aligned
  (Grid.hs:135 and :153 both use AllGridSizeKnown + SListI). 7bdd829 fixed that.

  Second, the three constraints are not actually redundant with each other -- they say
  different things, and collapsing them to one synonym would over-constrain APIs like
  'Applicative (Grid cs)' that only need the total size. The real defect is narrower and
  I found the mechanism: AllSizedKnown is a CLASS, so instance resolution discharges it
  from 'KnownNat n' per element and hands back the total size as a value-level Dict,
  whereas AllGridSizeKnown is a TYPE FAMILY that expands into the user's context. That
  single difference is what puts 'KnownNat (n GHC.* n)' in ../aoc/src/2025/04.hs:33 and
  ../aoc/src/2015/18.hs:31 while the FocusedGrid signatures right below them stay clean.
  Details and the two candidate fixes are in sized-grid-qh9.

title: SizedGrid/Internal/Type.hs is dead code containing an unsound axiom
description:
src/SizedGrid/Internal/Type.hs is imported by nothing. Verified:

    grep -rn 'SizedGrid.Internal' src tests sudoko/src gameOfLife/src ising-example/src
    -> only its own module header and module declaration

It is also absent from both 'exposed-modules' and 'other-modules' in sized-grid.cabal,
so cabal does not know about it at all (it would be omitted from an sdist).

Its contents are worth deleting rather than wiring up:

  - takeAddIsId (line 52-53):
        takeAddIsId :: forall m . Dict (((m - 1) + 1) ~ m)
        takeAddIsId = unsafeCoerce (Dict :: Dict (a ~ a))
    This is false at m = 0. It is an unsound axiom obtained by unsafeCoerce, and if
    anything ever imported it, it could be used to derive nonsense.

  - sLessThan (line 41-49) fabricates an SBool (n <=? m) via unsafeCoerce off a
    runtime Integer comparison. Sound in practice but the comment on 'magic'
    (line 55, 58) literally says 'don't really understand it' / 'Also don't understand'.

  - SBool/SBoolI duplicate what singletons or Data.Type.Bool already provide.

Action: delete the module. If a KnownNat-subtraction proof is needed later,
ghc-typelits-natnormalise supplies it soundly (see the plugin issue).

Also fix the cabal file to list every module -- the same audit should confirm nothing
else is missing.
close_reason: Module is no longer dead (windowFits + requiring are imported by Grid/Grid.hs) and is listed in the cabal file, so it was trimmed rather than deleted: removed the six unused definitions including the unsound takeAddIsId axiom, and closed the export list to (windowFits, requiring). Module audit clean; cabal check now warning-free; sdist builds and tests from scratch.

comments.author: Kevin Horlick
comments.text:
Reassessed. The issue's headline premise has gone stale in the meantime, but its
substance was right, so this became a trim rather than a delete.

WHAT CHANGED SINCE THIS WAS FILED
  - The module is no longer imported by nothing. 7bdd829 added
    'import SizedGrid.Internal.Type (windowFits)' to Grid/Grid.hs, and sized-grid-cpw
    has just added 'requiring' there too.
  - It is no longer absent from the cabal file. sized-grid-4c9 listed it under
    other-modules. That mattered more than it looked: with windowFits imported and the
    module unlisted, the sdist would have shipped a library that does not compile.
  - The suggested replacement for the axioms, ghc-typelits-natnormalise, is not
    available. sized-grid-h56 was retested today and deferred -- no GHC 9.14 release of
    ghc-tcplugins-extra exists upstream.

So 'delete the module' is off. What IS dead, verified by grepping src, tests, README.md
and all three example projects:

    SBool, SBoolI, sLessThan, takeAddIsId, magic, takeNat   -- 0 uses outside the module
    windowFits, requiring                                   -- live

DONE
  - Deleted all six dead definitions, takeAddIsId included. That was the important one:
    'Dict (((m - 1) + 1) ~ m)' is false at m = 0 and was obtained by unsafeCoerce, so it
    was a live footgun sitting in an internal module with no export list. Also gone are
    the two 'don't really understand it' comments on magic, and the SBool/SBoolI
    duplication of Data.Type.Bool.
  - Gave the module a closed export list of exactly (windowFits, requiring). windowFits
    is still an asserted axiom -- its soundness argument is in its haddock and rests on
    the 'x + z <= y + 1' constraint checked at every call site -- and an axiom reachable
    from more modules than need it is one waiting to be misused.
  - Dropped the now-unneeded Data.Proxy import.

MODULE AUDIT, the second half of this issue: clean. All 10 modules under src/ are
accounted for (9 exposed-modules + SizedGrid.Internal.Type in other-modules) and all 4
under tests/ (Main via main-is, three in other-modules). Nothing missing.

While there: 'cabal check' had one warning left, ChangeLog.md sitting in
extra-source-files instead of extra-doc-files. Moved it and README.md; README.lhs stays
in extra-source-files because it is the readme suite's main-is, i.e. build input rather
than documentation. 'cabal check' now reports no errors or warnings at all.

Verified: cabal build all warning-free, both suites green, 'cabal sdist' produces a
tarball containing every module.

title: Grid is boxed-vector only; no unboxed/storable representation for numeric grids
description:
src/SizedGrid/Grid/Grid.hs:40 hardcodes Data.Vector (boxed).

For the numeric workloads this library is aimed at, that is the wrong default:
  - ising-example/src/Main.hs is a Monte Carlo spin simulation
  - gameOfLife/src/Main.hs is a cellular automaton
  - ../aoc/src/2018/11.hs builds a 300x300 Int summed-area table
All of these want Data.Vector.Unboxed and get boxed Ints with a pointer chase each.

The complication: Functor/Applicative/Monad/Representable/Traversable all require the
element type to be unconstrained, so Grid cannot simply switch to Unboxed.

Options:
  1. Parameterise over the vector type:
       newtype GridOf v (cs :: [Type]) a = GridOf (v a)
       type Grid = GridOf V.Vector
     Keep the current instances for the boxed version; give the unboxed version the
     instances it can support (Foldable-like ops via a Vector.Generic constraint,
     no Functor). Costs an extra type parameter in every signature.
  2. Leave Grid boxed and add a separate SizedGrid.Grid.Unboxed with a monomorphic
     API (map/zipWith/fold/index taking Unbox constraints). Less elegant, far less
     disruptive, and covers the actual use cases.

Recommend option 2 first -- it is additive and non-breaking. Revisit 1 only if the
duplication becomes painful.

Prerequisite either way: benchmarks, so the win is measured rather than assumed.

title: Partial functions throughout: fromJust in coord arithmetic, error in complete pattern matches
description:
Two separate problems.

(a) 'error' calls that are genuinely unreachable but are there only because GHC cannot
see the ':|' pattern synonym is complete:
  - src/SizedGrid/Grid/Grid.hs:255   shrinkGrid _ = error "Impossible pattern in shrinkGrid"
  - src/SizedGrid/Coord.hs:319       weakenCoord _ = error "Unreachable pattern in weakenCoord"
  - src/SizedGrid/Coord.hs:333       strengthenCoord _ = error "Unreachable pattern in strengthenCoord"
  - src/SizedGrid/Coord.hs:203       error "Error in adding Coord. Should be unreachable"

Fix: add '{-# COMPLETE (:|) #-}' and '{-# COMPLETE EmptyCoord #-}' pragmas next to the
pattern synonyms in src/SizedGrid/Coord.hs:53-58. The dead equations then delete
cleanly and the warnings stay on. Cheap, zero risk, removes four error calls.

(b) 'fromJust . numToOrdinal' in arithmetic that is only total because of an invariant
GHC is not checking:
  - src/SizedGrid/Coord/Periodic.hs:48, 59, 70, 80
  - src/SizedGrid/Coord/HardWrap.hs:45, 61
  - src/SizedGrid/Ordinal.hs:82  (toEnum = fromJust . numToOrdinal)

These are 'correct' given mod/clamp, but they are also the hot path (see the Ordinal
representation issue) and they turn any future off-by-one into a crash with no
context. Switching Ordinal to a newtype over Int lets these become a single
'unsafeOrdinalFromInt' whose precondition is stated once and checked with an assert
in a debug build.
close_reason: Part (a) complete: COMPLETE pragmas removed three unreachable error equations, and the fourth was removed by switching Coord's AffineSpace instance to productTypeFrom/productTypeTo (a COMPLETE pragma cannot help there, evidence in comments). No 'error' remains in src/. Part (b), the fromJust sites, split out as sized-grid-j23 blocked on sized-grid-upo.

comments.author: Kevin Horlick
comments.text:
PART (a) DONE -- all four unreachable 'error' calls are gone. 'grep -rn "error \"" src/'
now returns nothing.

Three of them went exactly as this issue predicted. Added next to the pattern synonyms
in Coord.hs:

    {-# COMPLETE (:|) #-}
    {-# COMPLETE EmptyCoord #-}

after which the fallback equations in weakenCoord (Coord.hs), strengthenCoord
(Coord.hs) and shrinkGrid (Grid/Grid.hs) delete cleanly with -Wincomplete-patterns
still on. Cheap and zero risk, as advertised.

The fourth needed a different fix, and the one this issue proposed would not have
worked. In the AffineSpace instance for Coord, ('.+^') matched 'from b' against
'SOP (SOP.Z bs)' with an error fallback. No COMPLETE pragma helps there -- the scrutinee
is a generics-sop sum, and although 'IsProductType (CoordDiff cs) (MapDiff cs)' does
give 'Code (CoordDiff cs) ~ \'[MapDiff cs]' as a given, GHC will not reduce the type
family application far enough to see that the 'SOP.S' arm would have to hold an
'NS I \'[]'. Confirmed by deleting the fallback and getting:

    warning: [-Wincomplete-patterns] Pattern match(es) are non-exhaustive
      Patterns of type 'SOP I (Code (CoordDiff cs))' not matched: SOP (SOP.S _)

Fixed by not building the sum in the first place: generics-sop exports
'productTypeFrom :: IsProductType a xs => a -> NP I xs' and its inverse 'productTypeTo',
which go straight to and from the NP. ('.+^') and ('.-.') now use those instead of the
generic 'from'/'to' plus manual SOP/Z plumbing. Shorter, and there is no unreachable
branch left to write.

PART (b), the fromJust call sites, is SPLIT OUT as sized-grid-j23, which depends on
sized-grid-upo. Reason: this issue already says the real fix is a single
'unsafeOrdinalFromInt' with an asserted precondition, and that only exists once Ordinal
is a newtype over Int. Patching the seven sites now means writing the same defensive
code twice. There are eight, incidentally, not seven -- Coord/Class.hs:83 maxCoord was
missed in the original list.

Verified: cabal build all warning-free, both suites green.
